title: Diabetic ketoacidosis
stem: Resus 3. Miss Tsang, 19, with type 1 diabetes, has vomited for a day and is drowsy and breathing deeply. HR 124, BP 98/60, RR 32, SpO2 99%, temperature 37.8 °C. Capillary glucose reads 'HI'. Manage her.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: Monitoring on, then assess her yourself and confirm the diagnosis.

phases.title: Fluid and insulin
phases.goal: The first litre, then fixed-rate insulin for her weight.

phases.title: Potassium and glucose
phases.goal: Potassium in the next litre; dextrose when the glucose falls.

notes:
Checked against the Joint British Diabetes Societies (JBDS-IP) guideline 'The management of diabetic ketoacidosis in adults' (2023 update) and ADA 2024 hyperglycaemic crises consensus.

Diagnosis: ketonaemia 3.0 mmol/L or more (or significant ketonuria), glucose over 11 mmol/L or known diabetes, and bicarbonate under 15 or venous pH under 7.3 (JBDS 2023; euglycaemic DKA exists, e.g. with SGLT2 inhibitors). Severe: pH under 7.0, bicarbonate under 5, ketones over 6, K under 3.5 on admission, GCS under 12, SpO2 under 92%, systolic under 90, HR over 100 or under 60, anion gap over 16.

Fluids: 0.9% saline 1 L over 1 hour (if systolic under 90: 500 mL bolus over 10–15 minutes, repeat), then 1 L over 2 h, 2 h, 4 h, 4 h, 6 h (slower in the young, old, heart or renal failure). Potassium: none in the first litre usually; then 40 mmol/L if K 3.5–5.5; none if over 5.5; senior review if under 3.5. Insulin: fixed-rate IV insulin infusion 0.1 unit/kg/h (continue the patient's long-acting insulin). Add 10% glucose at 125 mL/h when glucose falls under 14 mmol/L. Targets: ketones down by 0.5 mmol/L/h, bicarbonate up 3 mmol/L/h, glucose down 3 mmol/L/h, K 4–5.5. Look for the precipitant (infection, missed insulin, MI, pregnancy). Resolution: ketones under 0.6 and pH over 7.3. Avoid bicarbonate; cerebral oedema risk in the young — watch for headache and falling GCS.

Your notes list DKA as a Medical gym topic without detail.

steps.label: Monitoring
steps.hint: Ask the nurse to put the patient on the monitor.

opts.t: Put her on the monitor: ECG leads, NIBP cuff and SpO2 probe.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

ABCDE.r: Dry mucosa, CRT 3 s, cool peripheries.

Precipitant.r: Ran out of insulin 3 days ago; burning when passing urine; LMP 2 weeks ago.

steps.label: Tests
steps.hint: Venous gas, blood ketones, U&E, FBC, cultures, urine, ECG, pregnancy test.

Now.r: pH 7.08, bicarbonate 7, K 5.8, Na 131, lactate 2.1, glucose 32.
Now.mark: Venous gas: severe acidosis and potassium

Other.t: U&E, FBC, CRP, blood and urine cultures, urine hCG
Other.r: Creatinine 140, WCC 17; urine nitrites positive; hCG negative.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Fluid first: the first litre over an hour.

opts.r: Too fast in a young adult: cerebral oedema risk. 1 L over the first hour, then slower.
Too slow for her deficit: 1 L over the first hour.
Not recommended: it worsens hypokalaemia and may raise cerebral oedema risk.
opts.t: Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 100 mL for the pH of 7.08

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Fixed-rate insulin for her weight; keep her long-acting insulin.

opts.mark: Fixed-rate insulin at 0.1 unit/kg/h and continue basal insulin
opts.t: Insulin (fixed-rate infusion) 0.1 unit/kg/h: 5.5 units/h for 55 kg

opts.r: Five times too much: 0.1 unit/kg/h. Hypoglycaemia and hypokalaemia follow.
Treat the ketones, not the glucose: keep the fixed-rate insulin running with glucose until ketones clear.
opts.t: Insulin (fixed-rate infusion) 10 units IV bolus, stopped when glucose is normal
opts.dose: 10 units IV bolus, stopped when glucose is normal

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: The second litre, with potassium once it is under 5.5.

opts.t: Potassium chloride 40 mmol/L in the next litre (K under 5.5)
opts.dose: 40 mmol/L in the next litre (K under 5.5)

opts.r: Never push potassium: cardiac arrest. 40 mmol in a litre.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Glucose falling: add dextrose and keep the insulin running.

opts.early: Not until the glucose is below 14.

opts.t: Hourly glucose and ketones; venous gas at 1, 2 and 4 hours
Treat the UTI; urinary catheter if oliguric; VTE prophylaxis
opts.mark: Treats the precipitant and supportive care

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: Severe DKA: HDU and the diabetes team.

opts.t: Medical team and HDU: severe DKA (pH 7.08, ketones 6.4, GCS 13); diabetes specialist team
opts.mark: Refers severe DKA to HDU and the diabetes team

badge.name: Ketone Crusher
badge.flavor: Saline, 0.1 unit/kg/h, K by level, glucose under 14. Treat the ketones.

cards.q: JBDS diagnosis of DKA includes ketones of…
cards.why: Plus acidosis (pH < 7.3 or HCO3 < 15) and glucose > 11 or known diabetes.

options: Hartmann's 5 L as fast as possible
cards.why: Give a 500 mL bolus first if systolic BP is under 90 mmHg.

cards.q: Potassium is withheld from fluids if K is…
options: Potassium is always given, at 40 mmol/L

cards.why: Measure ketones even if glucose is modest.

cards.q: Should long-acting insulin be continued during DKA?
cards.why: Prevents rebound ketosis when the infusion stops.
